those who have ever inherited the kingdom of God.
Especially unclean, effeminate men, men who sleep with males, and anyone who defiles themselves in any way,
whether male or female, in any of their unions that take place in this life of ours
here, and anyone who practices deception anywhere before God, secretly or openly.
If you do not see yourselves like Satan in the blazing furnace of fire,
being punished together in the underworld,
then all your deeds and all your plans are true,
and the words of the one saying these things are lies.
By the same author.
Therefore, let us not renounce only to refuse to bear with one another, lest God become angry with us. For we have not yet spent long bearing with one another, as
the Lord and his Christ and his holy angels have borne with us from the beginning of creation until this very day, and will forever.
Instead, let us serve one another as slaves, like Jesus, who took the form of a slave for our sake,
and like Paul, the slave of Jesus,
and like all the apostles and all the prophets, who became slaves of the Lord, his Christ Jesus,
according to the Scriptures: “I sent you my slaves the prophets at daybreak, early in the morning, and I sent them, but you did not listen.”
Did the prophets and the apostles serve the Lord or his Christ in [?], joining together to suffer with others and to die for the name of Jesus?
Therefore, when the Lord Jesus knew beforehand that our fathers the apostles would do everything he had commanded them, as he was about to leave them and go up to heaven according to the Scriptures,
just as they had also fulfilled what he had commanded them from the beginning, while the Lord of glory, Jesus, was with them,
he therefore said to them, “I will no longer call you my slaves, because a slave does not know what his master is doing.
Instead, I will call you my brothers and my friends, because I have told you everything I heard from my Father.”
“You did not choose me,” he said,
“but I chose you.
And I am sending you like sheep among wolves.
Do not be afraid of those who will kill your body.
If they persecuted me, they will persecute you.”
If they kept my word, they will keep yours too.

Letter of Shenoute.
Abraham our father wanted to have children by Sarah.
And Sarah wanted to have children by Abraham.
And this is how the Lord God gave Abraham a son in his old age:
he fathered Isaac by Sarah in her old age.
He became a beloved son to them, like ten thousand sons, though he was only one.
[?] is [?] after his [?]
who came from his own body.
He also gave comfort to the mother who had borne him.
And in this way he inherited his parents’ inheritance,
according to what was said to Abraham by God:
“That one, who is Ishmael, will not be your heir.
Nevertheless, I will also bless him for your sake
and greatly increase his numbers
and make him into a great and numerous nation.
And the one who comes from your [?]
Isaac is the one who will be your heir.
For this very reason, she spoke boldly, in the knowledge of God—
the mother of the son in her care—
saying, “Drive out this slave woman and her son,
for this slave woman’s son must not inherit along with my son Isaac.”
Isaac prayed to the Lord, wanting to have children by Rebekah.
And Rebekah wanted to have children by Isaac.
And this is how the Lord God gave them what their hearts desired,
fulfilling all their requests,
and they had Esau and Jacob.
Now Isaac blessed Jacob through God, following the advice of Rebekah, Jacob’s mother.
And Esau became Jacob’s servant, according to the Scriptures:
“The older will serve the younger.”
And again: “I loved Jacob, but I hated Esau.”
Now Jacob wanted to have children by Rachel,
like those he had by Leah
and those he had by Zilpah and Bilhah.
Rachel, too, wanted to have children by Jacob,
and she was distressed,
finding fault with Jacob in her ignorance,
in her overwhelming grief,
saying, “Give me children, or else I will die.”
And Jacob would say to her indignantly,
“Am I the Lord, I [?]?”
And Jacob said this in anger because he too wanted to have children by Rachel.
And so God saw their distress
and gave Jacob children by Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
And Jacob blessed all his children through the Lord God,
who blessed Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the children.
Therefore it is foolishness and blindness on our part
if some among us begin, in contentiousness and disobedience, to reject responsibilities they are able to take care of,
whether people entrusted to them, or ministries, or indeed any good work.
which we will be able to do for one another through God, for the salvation of our souls.
But it is also extreme foolishness and wicked stubbornness
if some among you choose to be barren through God and, with contentiousness and ignorance, refuse tasks
that they are capable of attending to—whether people, services, or any good work that you are to do for one another in the fear of the Lord.
Now if a woman who lives with a husband in the flesh desires to have sons and daughters,
and if Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah, and the mother of the prophet Samson,
and Elizabeth, the mother of John, who was filled with the Holy Spirit while still in his mother's womb—
if these and other holy women of ancient times cried out to the Lord, praying and pleading not to remain barren,
then if some among you reject people who have been entrusted to them by God,
how destitute they will be, because they have chosen to be barren and widowed!
For from the beginning until now, there have been many parents, both male and female, whom God has put to shame
because they were unwilling to take pains with others so that, through God, they might have them as sons and daughters.
But because of bodily comfort and pride, many men have refused to take pains with others through God,
just as others in turn took pains with them.
And many women have refused to take pains with others through God,
just as others in turn took pains with them.
And because of their pride and their love of bodily comfort, they have chosen to be barren,
and for the Lord to shut the doors of their soul like those of a barren woman,
and to make the counsels of instruction dry up within us like dry breasts, so that from that time on they can no longer teach others through God.
But from the beginning until now, there have also been many of our parents, both male and female, whom the Lord has blessed
because they preferred to take pains with others through God,
like our parents of ancient times, and the prophets and apostles, who became fathers of great multitudes through God,
and like Deborah, who became a judge and a mother in Israel, and like Huldah the prophetess,
whom the righteous King Josiah consulted, to inquire of the Lord through her, and like Anna, the daughter of Phanuel.
This is not the time for the parents of sons and daughters through God to say in their ignorance:
“The Lord will give eunuchs and virgins a choice place and a reputation better than sons and daughters.”
Some among us may choose this for themselves, in our community or in yours,
so that they renounce those who have attached themselves to them and do not care for them, saying:
“We are going to please God,
and these people and those others are not our concern.”
And in their stubbornness they bring in the prophet’s words,
interpreting them according to their hearts’ desires and their own comfort, saying,
“The Lord will give eunuchs and virgins the kingdom of heaven.”
And in this way they renounce others so that they do not have to care for them.
[?], saying, “[?] him.”
For they have never learned from the apostle, who says:
“Let no one seek his own advantage, but that of someone else.”
just as he himself did not seek his own benefit, but that of the many,
so that they might be saved.
Especially the prophet whose words these ignorant people interpret according to their own desires:
For the Lord will give the [?] a place [?] of renown, better than sons and daughters.
Isaiah himself, too, not only suffered many hardships for God’s name,
but also died for great multitudes and for all of us.
A father or mother who has sons and daughters, grandchildren, and many possessions,
And they are compelled by the affairs of life, so that they can never turn away from sons and daughters and all the other affairs of this age.
and also take charge of sons and daughters through God, and all the other works of righteousness.
For people like these cannot serve those who belong to them according to the flesh
and also serve others through God.
But people who, on the other hand, have no sons and daughters according to the flesh,
Or else, they have [?] and renounce [?]
[?] as is fitting.
of the calling of the one who called them to this life.
These are the eunuchs and the virgins—that is, you, brothers and sisters, and everyone who practices self-control everywhere
throughout the whole earth, whether those who do not know what honorable marriage and an undefiled bed are, or those who have taken wives and those who have taken husbands.
And when they became willing through God, following the counsel of the one who said
not to retaliate against those who kill them and flog them, just as they drag them
and throw them outside the city,
and everything they do to them in the synagogues and the councils,
and how they bring them before governors and kings, and great sufferings even to the point of death.
So, as we remember the sufferings of all these saints,
and consider how our Lord Jesus despised shame,
enduring the cross for the salvation of us all,
because he is our Savior, he is our Lord and our Father,
we also know this: the good and compassionate God bears with us all, from one end of the earth to the other end of the inhabited world,
from the beginning, when he created humanity on the earth, down to this very day.
And he will continue to bear with us until the end of the age, in the abundance of his mercy,
because we are his servants, and he is our ruler and our king.
Therefore, let us not renounce bearing with one another, so that God will not become angry with us. For we have not yet spent long bearing with one another as the Lord and his Christ have,
along with his holy angels, who bear with us from the beginning of creation down to this very day, and forever as well.
Instead, let us serve one another like Jesus, who took the form of a servant for our sake,
and like Paul, the servant of Jesus,
and like all the apostles and all the prophets, who became servants of the Lord and his Christ Jesus,
according to the Scriptures: “I sent my servants the prophets to you by day, at an early hour, and I sent them, and you did not listen.”
How did the prophets and the apostles serve the Lord or his Christ, except by choosing for themselves to suffer with others and to die for the name of Jesus?
Therefore, when the Lord Jesus knew beforehand that our fathers, the apostles, would do everything he had commanded them,
as he was about to leave them and go up to heaven, according to the Scriptures.
And likewise, how they fulfilled what he had commanded them from the beginning, while the Lord of glory, Jesus, was with them.
For this reason he said to them, “From now on I will no longer call you my slaves, because a slave does not know what his master is doing.
Instead, I will call you my brothers and my friends, because I have told you everything I heard from my Father.
It was not you,” he said, “who chose me.
Rather, I chose you.
And I am sending you out like sheep among wolves.
Do not be afraid of those who will kill your body.
If they persecuted me, they will persecute you.
If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they harass the members of his household with mockery and contempt!”
See now, brothers, how humbled we are, for our fathers, the prophets and the apostles, carried out great labors in abundant service,
among the wicked and the good, and among those who hated them and those who loved them.
Yet we, for our part, are not ashamed to say,
“We will not take care of our brothers,”
showing ourselves unworthy of the grace of the Lord, who made us worthy to be brought near to him through deeds
of which we are not worthy.
For this reason, do not let anyone among us, or among you yourselves, squander the grace of the Lord
and run away from others to whom they have been entrusted by God to be cared for,
just as others, in turn, took care of them from the beginning.
And even now, others take care of them in everything, whether in instruction in the Scriptures or in food
and clothing, and also in their sickness and in all the things in which those who care for them serve them as slaves.
For this reason, let us not say falsely, “Those who rule over us are our masters,
and we are under them like slaves.”
It is not those who rule over us who are above us.
But we are the ones above them, and they are the ones beneath us.
Or they are our slaves because they take care of us in everything through God.
How did the prophets, the apostles, and all the saints, from the beginning until now, willingly become slaves to others so that they too might receive life?
Was it not because they saw Jesus, the Lord of glory, taking the form of a slave for our sake?
And again, from the beginning God became a worker like a slave, although he is the Lord and the King.
Just as he made his angels spirits, as it is written.
And just as he created everything out of what did not exist.
He brought them all into being—the heavens, the earth, and everything in them—according to the Scriptures.
“You laid the foundation of the earth.
The heavens are the works of your hands.”
And again, just as he spoke so that all things would come into being.
And they all came into being at his command:
the cattle and the sheep, all the other animals of the field, and all the birds of the sky,
and the creatures in the waters of the rivers, the trees that bear fruit, and everything that grows up from the earth, according to the Scriptures.
And again, just as God took some earth from the ground, after consulting with Jesus, the firstborn of all creation,
who exists before them all, saying, “Let us make a human being in our image and according to our likeness.”
And when they had created the human being in their image and according to their likeness, according to the Scriptures,
God breathed into his face the breath of life.
The human being became a living soul.
God created them male and female, as it is written.
And just as God planted a garden in Eden, he placed this man there [?]
And among you.
So that we will truly become children of Abraham and children of all our ancient ancestors,
whom the Lord blessed,
because they loved not only their sons and daughters according to the flesh, but also all those who belonged to them.
But they loved everyone who believes in God and keeps God's commandments.
And in this way their descendants inherited everyone who would be faithful and righteous,
from the beginning until this very day, and forever.
But if our ancestors had disobedient and sinful children,
they did not reject their righteous children and make them flee from them
because of the increasing unruliness of the wicked children.
Instead, they cut off the sinful children from themselves.
They stayed with their righteous children all the days of their lives.
Therefore, just as many sinful children grieved our ancestors,
so too many righteous children made them glad.
And just as God often became angry enough to wipe out many ancient peoples because of the many sinful children among them,
so too God often turned his anger away from many ancient peoples because of the righteous children who were among them.
And just as great multitudes died in their ungodliness, amid every kind of lawlessness, because of many false prophets
who arose among many ancient peoples, justifying them and misleading them, bringing God's anger down upon them along with themselves,
so too great multitudes lived in every kind of righteousness because of many prophets of the Lord God
who arose among many ancient peoples, speaking the truth,
rebuking those who sinned and calling those who did good blessed.
And just as those who misled them came from among the ancient peoples—namely, false prophets and priests who led people astray—
so too the prophets of the Lord God came from among the ancient peoples, namely:
Moses, Joshua the prophet, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel,
and all the prophets who rebuked everyone who had sinned or would sin before the Lord,
and encouraged everyone who had practiced or would practice every kind of righteousness.
Now all the prophets of the Lord God and the apostles of our Lord Jesus
are all descendants of our father Abraham.
And they did not spare Abraham's descendants when they sinned before God, who created them.
But they brought great curses down upon their own brothers,
according to everything written in the Law of Moses.
And they also blessed everyone who honored the Lord God through their righteous deeds.
But above all, they cursed every false prophet, all the priests who lead people astray, and every antichrist,
and all false teachers and everyone who has refused to believe in our Lord Jesus, from the beginning until now.
Now if all the prophets, all the apostles, all our ancient fathers, and all the righteous from the beginning to this very day
are people who practice the truth and speak the truth,
because the truth is within them,
and this is how they were set right in all their deeds through God,
then let us too, brothers, practice the truth and speak the truth, so that we may be upright in all our deeds,
and so that we may be counted among the prophets, the apostles, and all the saints,
and become worthy of God, because God is truth.
And our Lord Jesus is truth, the one who said, “I am the truth.”
Therefore, let us not tell lies
about the evil deeds we do in the darkness,
so that we may not be counted among those who belong to Satan,
in whom there is no truth,
because he is a liar,
and who has never stood firm in the truth.
That is indeed why he is cursed, speaking lies and committing every sin among those who belong to him, as it is written:
“Whenever the liar speaks, he speaks from what is his own.” Understand, then, that everyone who commits sin and tells lies is counted among [?]
Satan.
Nor should we become traitors and thieves, so that we may not become like Judas, about whom he said through the Holy Spirit:
“Let the curse enter his belly like water, and like oil into his bones.”
Therefore, let us not be deceitful people before the Lord in any evil deed,
whether in defilement and impurity, in theft and lies, in hatred and hostility toward others, or in hypocrisy and empty glory.
Who are those who are hostile toward others, if not those who grumble?
and shaking their heads, with their necks held high and their eyes rolling at those who govern them,
who take care of them and teach them
to be well disciplined in all God's commands.
Who are the hypocrites except people who have people [?] toward them, covering up for those who commit transgression through every kind of wrongdoing?
Therefore, let us not go astray through falsehood and cover up one another's sins.
For this is the downfall of every congregation that has sinned before God from the beginning down to this very day.
Instead, let us earnestly teach one another not to sin before the Lord.
And again, if we go astray and commit some wrongdoing, let us firmly rebuke one another,
for this is the strength and preservation of every congregation that has pleased the Lord from the beginning until now.
It is no surprise if we become like the false prophets and cover up one another's sins,
and God pours out his curse upon us in anger and wrath.
Rather, the wonder is if we follow the example of our fathers, the prophets and the apostles,
and keep teaching one another not to sin before God,
and again, even if we commit some wrongdoing in ignorance, we firmly rebuke one another so that we repent,
so that the Lord may pour out his blessing upon us in mercy and compassion.
Nevertheless, although it is fitting for us to say many things to you in this letter,
it is also fitting for us to stop,
and entrust you to God and to all the words of the Scriptures, as the apostle says:
“I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and give you the inheritance with all the saints.”
Now then, since you sent word to us,
“The sister whom you appointed in place of the one who died has refused the work you assigned her,”
we want you to tell us why she stopped carrying out the duty you assigned her,
so that, if we learn that she refused because she cannot bear the work assigned to her, she may rest in peace in the place where she lived before.
But if, instead, she refused out of contentiousness and lack of discipline,
then she herself is lying before the Lord.
that I broke my commitment, saying, “I cannot do this.”
And after some days, or after some time, if we hear that she has broken her commitment dishonestly, you will all find out what we will do to her,
because she did not tell us how they had treated her violently,
or in what matter they had mistreated her.
If, on the other hand, we find that others are preventing her from telling the truth, what we will do to these others will not be hidden from you either,
because they and she have made a covenant with falsehood through Satan’s counsel.
After this, look, I have sent the old man to you,
so that you will remember God and have compassion on yourselves in your own community, and on us too in ours,
and tell us about all these wrongdoings among you.
For we have been weighed down with sorrow, both we and you.
But people who have no sons or daughters according to the flesh,
or who do have them but renounce them,
along with many possessions, wishing to live worthily of the calling
of the one who called them to this way of life—
these are the eunuchs and the virgins, namely you, brothers, and everyone who practices self-restraint everywhere throughout the earth,
whether those who do not know what honorable marriage and the pure marriage bed are, or those who have taken wives and those who have taken husbands and then became willing,
through God, following the counsel of the one who said,
“Whoever can bear it, let him bear it,”
and renounced honorable marriage and the pure marriage bed,
and renounced their sons and daughters, their siblings and parents, and everything they possessed,
remembering the Lord’s saying,
“Whoever comes to me hating his father and mother, his children, his brothers and sisters, and even his own life.”
People like these are the ones who will be able to become disciples of the Lord according to the Scriptures.
And these are the eunuchs who have no children according to the flesh,
but have become fathers of many children of God.
Because, whether they have no children or, on the other hand, they do, they have renounced them all, along with everything they own.
They have taken up their cross and followed the Lord.
Our holy fathers, the prophets and the apostles, were like this.
These are the ones who truly became eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of God.
And this is how they became fathers of many peoples, according to the Lord’s saying:

“Everyone who has left behind a house, a brother, a sister, a father, a mother, a wife, a son, a daughter, or a field for the sake of my name will receive them many times over and inherit eternal life.”
Therefore, brothers, let none of us burden his neighbor with the attitude of estrangement within us, being divided in our hearts toward one another.
For they compel us, through our thoughts of being wise for ourselves alone, not to care for one another.
Instead, as fellow workers of God,
let each of us support his neighbor, whether great or small.
And let us love living together in peace,
without sin or deceit, like God and his angels who dwell in heaven.
What sensible children would not wish to do the things their righteous father does?
What wise brothers would not follow the example of their faithful brothers who are their elders?
That is to say, what wise people would not wish to do the deeds their Father in heaven does,
that is, God and our Lord Jesus,
and follow the example of the Lord’s angels, the example of the prophets, and the example of Paul and all the apostles, who said:
“Follow our example, our purpose, our faith, our patience, our love, our endurance, our persecutions, and our sufferings.”
Then again: “We have given ourselves to you as an example.”
And again: “My brothers, take the prophets as an example of suffering and patience.”
Again: “You shall make yourself an example in everything.”
Then again: “Likewise, the older women, with holy conduct.”
Above all, Scripture tells us about our Lord Jesus:
“He is the one who left you an example so that you might follow in his footsteps.”
What is the work of God and our Lord Jesus, if not the works of his hands?
His hands are what molded us and made us.
For this reason, according to the Scriptures, God and our Lord Jesus are working for the salvation of every person right up to the present, according to the apostle’s words:
“Now the one who prepared us for this is God.”
What is the way of life of the angels in heaven,
if not to carry out their glorious works each day, blessing and glorifying God and our Lord Jesus,
and to perform services for those on earth so that they may inherit salvation?
What is the way of life of the prophets and the apostles, if not to choose for themselves to suffer with others, even to the point of death?
And in all these things they give thanks to the Lord [?], blessing those who curse them and praying for those who persecute them.
And they pray to God that he will not repay those who kill them and flog them, as they drag them away
and throw them outside the city,
along with everything they do to them in the synagogues and councils,
and the way they bring them before governors and kings, with great suffering, even to the point of death.
So, as we act
